To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) RNNs with action-conditioning outperform RNNs with conditioning only on user history, (b) the action module can be trained using the data of deployed recommender systems, (c) the state-action fusion is essential for performance.
(1) we extend RNNs to incorporate the action of recommendation, and (2) the proposed models outperform the state-of-the-art baselines.
\textit{we propose a novel approach for next item recommendation that takes into account interactions with recommended items.}
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of next item recommendation in online services.
the development and evaluation of RNN architectures for recommendation that can take into account the effect of deployed recommendation system on user behavior.
the problem of sequential recommendation in the presence of recommendations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model outperforms the baseline in terms of the next item prediction.
our proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines in terms of next-item prediction task.
the proposed method is able to learn the user’s sequential behavior and improve the next-item prediction task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new framework that takes into account user interactions with recommended items and we evaluate its performance on real-world datasets.
the recommendation actions can be used to enhance the next item prediction performance.
we are the first to consider action-conditional sequence modeling for recommendation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
modeling user interaction with recommendations is important for accurate prediction.
the action-conditional RNN architectures are able to learn the user behavior dynamics in a more robust way.
the action module can be incorporated in the RNN framework to model user interactions with recommended items, and this can improve performance of the next item prediction.
